turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
Doctor: Hello, I’m your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: I’m here for my annual blood pressure check. I also have occasional knee pain from osteoarthritis, but otherwise I feel fine.
Are you currently experiencing any symptoms such as severe headache, chest pain, shortness of breath, vision changes, weakness, or confusion?
Patient: No, I’m not having severe headaches, chest pain, shortness of breath, vision changes, weakness, or confusion—just the occasional knee pain.
What is your blood pressure reading today, and do you know what it has been running at home recently?
Patient: My blood pressure reading today is around 138/82, and at home it’s usually in the same range—roughly 130s to 140s over 70s to low 80s.
Are you currently taking any prescription medications to treat your blood pressure, or any other regular medications?
Patient: Yes—I'm taking my prescribed blood pressure medication regularly. Other than that, I only use acetaminophen occasionally for my knee pain.
Do you have a history of diabetes, high cholesterol, kidney disease, heart disease, or stroke, and when was your last blood work done?
Patient: I don’t have diabetes, high cholesterol, kidney disease, heart disease, or a history of stroke. My last blood work was done as part of my routine checkup about a year ago.
What is the name and dose of the blood pressure medication you are currently taking?
Patient: I’m currently taking lisinopril, 10 mg once daily.
Have you noticed any side effects from the lisinopril, such as a dry cough, swelling of your lips or tongue, dizziness when standing, or decreased urination?
Patient: No, I haven’t noticed any dry cough, swelling of my lips or tongue, dizziness when standing, or any change in my urination.
Do you smoke cigarettes, vape, or use any tobacco products, and if so, how much per day?
Patient: No, I don’t smoke or vape, and I don’t use any tobacco products.
Do you have a family history of high blood pressure, heart attack, or stroke in your parents or siblings, particularly before age 55 for men or 65 for women?

Patient: My brother passed away from a blood cancer, but I don’t recall any early heart attack or stroke in my parents or siblings before those ages. I don’t have a strong family history of high blood pressure either.
Are you taking any over-the-counter medications besides acetaminophen for your knee pain, such as ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin), naproxen (Aleve), or any decongestants for colds/allergies?
Patient: No, I don’t take ibuprofen, naproxen, or any cold/allergy decongestants—just acetaminophen occasionally for my knee pain.
How many alcoholic beverages do you typically consume per week?
Patient: I don’t drink alcohol regularly—if anything, it’s only an occasional drink, maybe once a month at most.
How would you describe your typical weekly physical activity level—for example, how many days per week do you engage in moderate exercise like brisk walking?
Patient: I exercise daily, usually brisk walking or similar moderate activity for about 30–60 minutes most days of the week. I’d say I get moderate exercise nearly every day.
Do you snore loudly, or has anyone observed you having pauses in breathing or gasping during your sleep?
Patient: No, I don’t snore loudly, and I haven’t been told that I stop breathing or gasp during sleep.
What is your typical daily diet like regarding salt intake—do you frequently eat processed foods, canned soups, deli meats, or add salt to your meals?
Patient: I mostly cook at home and eat a lot of vegetables, and I don’t add much salt to my meals. I rarely eat processed or deli foods, and I don’t usually have canned soups.
